query: deep premortem on evals/files/plans/2026-10-01-cron-host-move.md. Job code is in evals/files/jobs, migration in evals/files/migrations. I start Friday.
expected_behavior: Flags as a HIGH tiger that both crontabs are active from Friday 18:00 to Monday 09:00, so send_digest.py runs twice per night and emails every subscriber twice, because send_digest.py has no check or lock against a second run for the same day.
Flags as a tiger or elephant that jobs/crontab.old runs a fourth job the plan never moves: expire_sessions.py every 15 minutes, so sessions stop expiring once app-vm-01 is retired

Each tiger carries an explicit statement of the mitigation that was looked for and NOT found (a mitigation_checked field or an equivalent 'checked: no X, no Y' line), for example no unique constraint, no lock and no already-sent check for the digest.

Classifies the hardcoded TEMPLATE_DIR path /var/app/digest/templates in send_digest.py as a paper tiger or false alarm, not a tiger, and cites the os.path.exists fallback to the templates folder next to the code.
Classifies the 0007 migration on the ~40M-row digest_log table as a paper tiger or false alarm, not a tiger, because it uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.

Ends by asking Dave to choose how to proceed with these options or close equivalents: accept the risks and proceed, add mitigations to the plan (marked as recommended), research mitigation options, or discuss specific risks.

query: Before I build this, how does it blow up in prod? evals/files/token-cache/plan.md, client is evals/files/token-cache/token_client.ts
expected_behavior: Sorts the risks into three named groups: tigers, paper tigers and elephants.
Flags as a tiger that the refresh token is stored under the same Redis key with TTL = expires_in, so when the key expires the refresh token is lost too and no worker can refresh.

Flags as a tiger that several workers can miss the cache at once and each call refreshToken with the same refresh token; because the partner rotates refresh tokens, all but one refresh fail or invalidate each other.
Treats a hung or slow token endpoint as a paper tiger or false alarm, not a tiger, and cites the existing 5 s AbortSignal.timeout with 2 retries and backoff in token_client.ts.
States that HIGH-severity tigers block the build: each must be mitigated in the plan or explicitly accepted by Dave before implementation starts.
